snapshot_warning: PHASE A SNAPSHOT, TAKEN WHILE A BATCH OF AGENTS IS PUSHING TO THIS REPOSITORY. This is a point-in-time record, not a deletion list. Do not act on it. Phase B must collect its own observations -- one immediately before the deletion and one immediately after -- with scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs, and authorize against those. liveEligibility refuses outright without a freshly collected observation, and the invariants are compared between the two fresh observations, never against this file. This baseline is historical context: the repository goes on moving, and a Phase B compared against a Phase A snapshot would report ordinary progress as damage.
method: Read-only, and every asserted derivation is a command run by scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs with its command line, exit code, byte count and a SHA-256 of its raw stdout recorded beside the answer. That includes the graph facts, not only the repository queries around them: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against dev and main, `git rev-list --count` in both directions and for commits reaching neither line, `git rev-list` for the ids of the commits reaching neither line, one `git merge-base --is-ancestor` per tag reported by `git ls-remote --tags origin`, `git grep` over the whole tree, `git log -1`, and an all-state paginated `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls?state=all&head=<owner>:<branch>` per branch. Head lists are taken over two independent transports and cross-checked. Every list endpoint is paginated to the end, and each GitHub-wide search records whether it retrieved every result the API reported -- a truncated sweep establishes nothing and says so. No ref was created, deleted, renamed or force-pushed to produce this file.

What must not change across a deletion is compared between two observations collected either side of it (boundaryInvariantFindings); this baseline records what Phase A saw so a later reader can see how far the repository has moved since.

revision_history.note: Schema v2: the six-value classification, release-tag containment, superseding evidence, the reference scan, protection status, and a named list of what could not be established.
Schema v3: external facts moved behind a receipted collector, the destructive decision took a live observation, and the Phase B deletion log stopped being emitted in Phase A.

Schema v4, second remediation. The per-branch pull request history was read with `gh pr list --limit 200`, whose flag is a maximum: an omitted 201st historical pull request was indistinguishable from a branch that never had one, while the record asserted exactly that. It is a paginated REST read now, and both the collector and the consumers refuse a history that was read as a bounded slice, the same way they already refused a truncated search. And Phase A no longer ships an executor: performing a deletion, witnessing it and recording completion is the blocked phase's work, so what is here is the evidence and the verifiers -- liveEligibility, boundaryInvariantFindings, deletionLogFindings, prerequisiteFindings -- and nothing that deletes. Earlier in v4: The observation digest is now recursive: the previous one passed an array replacer to JSON.stringify, which is a key allowlist applied at every level, so every nested head, pull request and receipt hashed to the same value and the digest bound nothing. Every graph derivation a branch record asserts is now collected here with its own receipt -- previously the record asserted merge-base, rev-list, tag-contains, grep and PR-history results the collector never ran. List endpoints paginate to the end and searches prove completeness, so an open pull request on a second page can no longer read as absent. Calendar-impossible instants are rejected before any freshness arithmetic. The invariant comparison is now between two freshly collected observations bracketing the deletion instead of against this snapshot. And the after-snapshot head exception has to be earned by an open pull request rather than by appearing in a list.

Re-collected after PR #609 (#556) merged. A branch-audit snapshot is the fastest-staling artifact in this release, and this one was two merges old: taken against dev at fa0749959fffb8ccfabe7a8a0d6f5882a45b4dcf, it is now taken against 93179cf53757e0755efc1936c7d96c0779feedf1. The drift from 2026-09-03T05:41:47Z is one head and one number. task/issue-556-strict-confinement, audited ACTIVE as the head of open PR #609, merged and was removed by delete_branch_on_merge; it moves to previously_recorded_heads_now_absent and the audited set falls from four branches to three. dev advanced 63 commits, so behind_dev rises by 63 on all three survivors -- 307 to 370, 30 to 93, 255 to 318. Every other derived fact is unchanged: no survivor's ancestry, unique-commit count, release-tag containment, tree scan or reference sweep moved, and no recommendation changed. No schema change.

Schema v5, third remediation, re-collected at the head that merges after #609 and #614 are both in dev. Two changes move what the digest covers, which is why the observation is v3 and this file is v5. Tag containment is decided by one `git merge-base --is-ancestor` per tag and now cites the receipt for each of them: it cited whichever tag sorted first, whose recorded exit status was 1 -- 'not contained' -- beside a value listing seven tags the branch is contained in, and neither checker could see it, because one asked only whether the named receipt existed and the other compared the record against the same record. verifyObservation compares each cited command's exit status against the answer it is cited for now, in both directions. And the commits that reach neither dev nor main are collected as ids rather than only counted, because the SUPERSEDED route accepted any list of 40-hex strings of the right length as an accounting of them, which is the one route by which a branch holding unmerged work becomes deletion-eligible. Also in this revision: the Phase B contract names deletionAuthorizationFindings, and deletionLogFindings is handed the two observations it was previously asked to trust a record's citation of -- the composition this contract used to name returned no finding at all for a COMPLETED record citing two well-formed digests that named nothing, stamped forty days after the observation it calls the one collected immediately beforehand. And five prose sites here and in the rendered report described the collector as running `git tag --contains` and an all-state `gh pr list --head`, both of which this issue's work removed as unsafe and neither of which matches any receipt in this record.

lifecycle.note: The PR carrying this audit must not use a closing keyword for #572. It completes the read-only-audit phase; final-deletion is blocked on #578 and #588 and is the phase that produces the deletion log.

phase_b_contract.note: The Phase B output is `branch-deletion-log`, which the canonical execution plan reserves for the blocked final-deletion phase. No deletion log is emitted by this PR; what is recorded here is the contract that artifact has to satisfy.
phase_b_contract.prerequisite_authority: fixtures/execution-plan/github-state.json -- #578 and #588 must be closed there with close evidence. The deletion log does not clear its own prerequisites; scripts/branch-audit.mjs cross-checks its claims against that snapshot and treats a disagreement as a finding.
phase_b_contract.entry_point: deletionAuthorizationFindings({audit, log, pre, post, completion}) in scripts/branch-audit.mjs is the gate Phase B has to clear, and the only composition that binds the deletion record to the two observations it cites. Everything it needs is collected by scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs: an observation immediately before the deletion and another immediately after. Its read-only half is liveEligibility(audit, pre), which answers what would be eligible right now and why each of the rest would not be -- the ref still at the commit the audit judged, no pull request open on it according to either source that would know, and the observation reporting it unprotected. Phase A ships no executor: performing the deletion, witnessing it and recording completion is Phase B's work, and the verifiers below are what Phase B has to satisfy.
phase_b_contract.verifiers: deletionAuthorizationFindings({audit, log, pre, post, completion}) is the composition to run, and running it is not optional: it is the only caller that hands every check the evidence it compares against. It composes prerequisiteFindings(completion) for whether Phase B may start; verifyObservation and derivationFindings against the fresh observation; deletionLogFindings(log, {completion, pre, post}) for the record Phase B produces, which recomputes both observation digests and applies the OBSERVATION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS window rather than accepting the record's own citation of them; boundaryInvariantFindings(log, pre, post) for what must not have changed across the deletion; cleanupInvariantFindings and openPrHeadDeletionFindings for the stored half; and the live re-checks of every branch it is about to remove. liveEligibility(audit, pre) is the read-only report and may be run on its own, but it cannot check a deletion record and does not claim to. Phase A ships all of these and no code that deletes anything.

required_shape.completed_at: <instant, stamped by the gate between its two collections>
required_shape.deleted: [{name, sha}] -- the audit's eligible set narrowed to the branches the fresh observation still shows at the judged commit with no pull request open on them. An empty list is legitimate when nothing survives that narrowing, and then no_op_reason says why.
required_shape.blockers_cleared: [{issue, canonical_state}] -- cross-checked against the canonical snapshot, not believed
required_shape.pre_observation: {digest} -- the recursive digest of the observation collected immediately before the deletion. The gate recomputes it from that observation and refuses a record citing anything else, so a well-formed digest naming nothing is not a citation.
required_shape.post_observation: {digest} -- the recursive digest of the observation collected immediately after it, recomputed and compared the same way. Both instants are checked against completed_at, within OBSERVATION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (900s), so "immediately" is a condition rather than a word.

phase_b_contract.invariant_comparison: boundaryInvariantFindings(log, pre, post), reached through deletionAuthorizationFindings, over the two observations the gate collected itself: main, dev, tag ref and commit identity, the complete protection objects, the rulesets, the install source, the repository settings, and every open pull request head -- compared between the two fresh observations. The set of heads that vanished between them must equal exactly the set the log says it deleted.

repository_policy.note: The branch policy this issue asks to be written down. Descriptive of the repository's current settings where a setting exists, prescriptive where none does.
rules: feature/, task/ and fix/ branches are deleted once their PR merges. delete_branch_on_merge is enabled, so this happens automatically; the branches in this audit that were not removed are the ones that never had a PR.
tmp/* branches live at most seven days or until their task ends, whichever comes first. No setting enforces this; it is checked by re-running this audit.
release/ and hotfix/ branches are deleted after the release ships and the back-merge into dev lands.
main and dev are protected: no deletion, no force push, enforced for admins. No repository rulesets are configured.

A branch is not an evidence archive. Anything worth keeping is moved into a commit, a committed fixture, a document or an issue record before the branch it lived on is deleted -- which is why this issue's Phase B is blocked on #578 and #588 rather than running now.
